title: They work, more or less
text:
They work, more or less. I didn't want regular cooling racks that didn't stack because of my lack of counter space. These DID help with that problem. I usually put my smallest baking sheet underneath them to catch any crumbs that fall through.

I've only had a few instances where cookies get caught in the slats or fall through--for advertising against this exact problem, I think they could be better.

The legs do collapse easily. You have to be pretty careful to not bump them when you've got them all set up. That can be a little bit of a challenge as you're loading them I suppose. My cookie sheets all have lips on them so I don't slide them right off the cookie sheet anyway and just move them one by one--not a big deal for me.

I don't really understand why people whine about having to load them one at a time and then stack them. You saw the picture, what makes you think you'd be able to do it any other way?

Since one stacks on top of the other one you will have to be careful about placing cookies along the edges so you can put the next rack on top. That is probably the most annoying part because it limits the space on your tray even further. I often will let the cookies cool for a few minutes on the trays and then double or triple up layers of cookies to let them cool completely.

I'm not really sure what people were expecting here and why they sound so pissed. They're 3 cooling racks for 10 or 12 bucks, and most of the complaints were from people not paying attention. They work fine for me until I can get more counter space for cooling racks.
